output.situation: The user feels a sense of inadequacy compared to their peers who are hitting traditional milestones like marriage and homeownership. debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: You are currently defining your existence through the eyes of others. By measuring yourself against your friends, you are treating your life as an object to be evaluated rather than a project to be created. You have no blueprint; you must choose your own values.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: It is not that simple, Sartre. The user is trapped in a social field where these milestones are the primary markers of success. This feeling of being behind is a direct result of the cultural capital their peers are accumulating. It is a structural pressure, not just a personal failure.
debate.author: Pierre Bourdieu

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: Why concern yourself with the opinions or the possessions of others? If you do not desire the house or the marriage, then the race you feel behind in does not exist. Remember, it is not things that disturb us, but our judgment about them.
debate.author: Marcus Aurelius

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: Aurelius, indifference is a dangerous trap. If the user simply ignores these pressures, they risk falling into bad faith, convincing themselves they are free while actually just drifting. They must actively commit to a project that is their own, not just reject the projects of others.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: I concede my earlier point. I initially viewed this as mere social conditioning, but Sartre is right. The user must stop measuring their life by the metrics of the bourgeois family unit. They need to actively construct a new field of action that values different forms of capital.
debate.author: Pierre Bourdieu

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: Constructing a new field still keeps them tethered to the idea of status. If they seek to replace one set of external goals with another, they will always be chasing someone else's approval. True freedom is found in the internal life, regardless of what the world values.
debate.author: Marcus Aurelius

debate.speaker: The Existentialist
debate.text: But the internal life is empty without action. You cannot just meditate your way into a life. To be human is to be engaged. The user must decide what they want to build, even if it looks like nothing to their friends.
debate.author: Jean-Paul Sartre
debate.basis: Basis: Jean-Paul Sartre, Existentialism is a Humanism

debate.speaker: The Social Critic
debate.text: Exactly. The goal is not to be different for the sake of it, but to recognize that the game of milestones is a social construct. Once you see the game for what it is, you can choose to stop playing it and design your own life.
debate.author: Pierre Bourdieu

debate.speaker: The Stoic
debate.text: If they choose to stop playing, they will find peace. The only thing that matters is the quality of their own mind and their own actions. Everything else is indifferent.
debate.author: Marcus Aurelius
